subject: fluid_mechanics
title: Determine Coefficient of Discharge for Orifice Meter
aim: To determine the coefficient of discharge of the given orifice meter and to calibrate.
apparatus: A pipe fitted with a orifice meter
theory:
An orifice meter is a simple device used for measuring the discharge through pipes. It works on the principle same as that of venturi meter i.e. by reducing the cross sectional area of the flow passage a pressure difference between the two sections is developed and the measurement of the pressure differences enables the determination of the discharge through the pipe. It consists of a flat circular plate with a circular hole called orifice, which is concentric with the pipe axis. The thickness of the plate less than or equal to 0.05 times the diameter of the piece.

Formulas:
1. Actual Discharge Qact = Ah/t in m³/sec (A = L × B = 0.4 × 0.4 = 0.16 m², h = 0.05 m rise)
2. Theoretical Discharge Qth = {a1 a2 √(2gH)} / √(a1² - a2²) in m³/sec
3. Coefficient of Discharge Cd = Qact / Qth
Where H = head over the orifice meter in m = h_diff × 12.6
procedure: The internal dimensions of the collecting tank were measured (L = 0.4 m, B = 0.4 m).
Inlet valve of collecting tank was closed.
Water was allowed to rise of mercury in manometer.
Readings were taken down in both limbs of mercury in manometer (h1, h2).
Head of orifice meter was noted.
Inlet valve of collecting tank was opened.
Time taken for 5 cms (0.05 m) rise of water in collecting tank was noted.
Procedure was repeated for various heads over the orifice meter and the coefficient of discharge was calculated.

formulas.label: Manometer Differential (h)
formulas.derivation: Height differential of mercury column between upstream and downstream taps of the orifice plate.
formulas.purpose: Measures differential pressure drop across the orifice plate in meters of mercury.
formulas.practical_application: Differential pressure taps near orifice plates are standardized in ISO/ASME codes.

formulas.label: Total Water Head (H)
formulas.purpose: Converts differential height of mercury into equivalent meters of water column head.

variables.meaning: Total pressure head in meters of water

formulas.practical_application: Converts physical manometer heights into energy heads for Bernoulli equation calculations.

formulas.label: Actual Discharge (Qact)
formulas.derivation:
Qact = (L × B × 0.05) / t
Where L = 0.4 m, B = 0.4 m (Tank Area A = 0.16 m²), and h_rise = 0.05 m (5 cm rise). Thus Qact = 0.008 / t.
formulas.purpose: Calculates true flow rate entering the collecting tank.
formulas.practical_application: Gravimetric/volumetric tank measurements provide primary standards for flow calibration.

formulas.label: Theoretical Discharge (Qth)
formulas.derivation:
Derived from 1D energy equation between upstream pipe section (a1 = 3.46×10⁻⁴ m²) and orifice throat section (a2 = 1.26×10⁻⁴ m²).

Qth = (a1 a2 √(2gH)) / √(a1² - a2²)
formulas.purpose: Predicts ideal flow rate theoretical output assuming zero frictional head loss.
formulas.practical_application: Calculates primary flow index for standard orifice metering runs.

formulas.label: Coefficient of Discharge (Cd)
formulas.derivation: The ratio of measured actual flow Qact to theoretical prediction Qth.
formulas.purpose: Corrects theoretical discharge equation for jet contraction (vena contracta) and eddy dissipation losses.
formulas.practical_application: Orifice Cd (~0.62) is essential for oil & gas metering calculations.

calculation_steps.label: Step 1: Equivalent Pressure Head Over Orifice (H)

trial_inputs.label: Time for 5cm Rise
trial_inputs.tooltip: Time for 5 cm (0.05 m) water rise in tank

result_template: Coefficient of Discharge for orifice meter is found to be , Cd = {avg_Cd}
precautions: The sharp edge of the orifice plate must face upstream.
Purge all air bubbles from piezometer glass tubes and manometer lines before starting.
Read piezometer water levels at eye level to avoid meniscus reading errors.
